screens.prompt: Put the average of the two best times into C2, taking the values from the unsorted column.

hints.syntax: Two LARGE calls and an average: =(LARGE(B2:B6,1)+LARGE(B2:B6,2))/2.
hints.func-large: LARGE gives you one position at a time, so ask for two of them and average the pair.
hints.require-ref: Both LARGE calls read the same range, B2:B6, so no time is typed into the formula.
hints.value: The two best are 61 and 58, and their average is 59.5.
hints.error: Dividing by zero anywhere in the formula leaves #DIV/0!.

reject.why: the average of all five, 56.2, which includes the slow times
only the single best time, 61, so nothing has been averaged
Ben and Dev only, so the best two of the team are not in the range
the second best alone, 58, rather than the average of the pair
the second and third best, 57.5, which leaves the winner out
dividing by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the missing comma leaves LARGE with one unusable argument

screens.prompt: Put the place the middle time earns into C2, so the row shows where the median sits.

hints.func-median: The middle time is the median, and it is a value in the list, not a place in it.
hints.func-rank: Once you have the middle time, RANK turns it into a place.
hints.require-ref: Both functions read B2:B6, so the comparison stays inside the team.
hints.value: The median of the five times is 57, and 57 is third from the top.
hints.error: Dividing by zero leaves #DIV/0! in the cell instead of a place.

reject.why: the middle time itself, 57, rather than the place it earns
the mean, 56.2, which is not a time in the list and has no place
Ada's own place, 2 — nothing has been asked about the middle of the list
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
the range leaves out B2, so the median is of four swimmers rather than five
twice the place, 6, which is outside a list of five

docs.explain: A summary statistic answers a question, and most real questions need two of them joined together. The average of the best two times is not a function Excel has; it is LARGE asked twice and divided by two, and reading it as a sentence is the skill this lesson is really teaching. The second screen nests MEDIAN inside RANK so the answer is a place rather than a value: the middle time is 57, and the place that time earns is 3. Nesting works because every function returns a value that another function can consume, and the trace is read inside-out — MEDIAN finishes, then RANK uses what it returned. The trap is that a mean of a subset can produce a number that exists nowhere in the data, so it has no place, no row and no format to inherit; averaging the top two gives 59.5, which is not a swim time at all. Watch the ranges: two LARGE calls that point at different ranges silently average two different groups, which is the most common way a hand-built summary goes quietly wrong.

errors.text: A LARGE position went past the end of the range, so there is no value to include.
RANK was asked about a number that does not appear in the range, as a mean of a subset never will.
One of the nested arguments was text that cannot be read as a number.

docs.atWork: A selection report that averages a team's best two results, and a review sheet that shows where the median case sits in the ranked list.
docs.outcome: Join two summary functions into one answer, reading the nesting inside-out.
docs.dataset: One team's swim times summarised two ways
